item.title: Low-Frequency Charge Noise in Bilayer Graphene Quantum Dots
item.description:
Pay dirt new result — Extracted median charge-noise amplitude of Sμ1/2(1 Hz)=1.16 μeV/Hz in gate-defined bilayer graphene quantum dots, with a 10-90 percentile range of 0.41 μeV/Hz to 2.24 μeV/Hz.

Grade 0.485 · 2.5σ above the day's baseline · matched “Charge Noise Spectroscopy Using Coherent Exchange Oscillations in a Singlet-Tri…” · Jessica Richter, Max J. Ruckriegel, Jonas D. Gerber, Tijl Degroote, Christoph Adam, Markus Niese, Lara Ostertag, Clara Galante, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Petar Tomic, Artem O. Denisov, Hadrien Duprez, Klaus Ensslin, Thomas Ihn

Figure

Charge-noise amplitude Sμ1/2 at 1 Hz across bilayer graphene single dots, double dots, resonator readout, and TMD proximitized devices, benchmarked alongside literature values for GaAs, Si MOS, Si/SiGe, and Ge/SiGe.

Asks

How low-frequency charge noise in bilayer graphene quantum dots compares to established semiconductor qubit platforms and how it behaves across tuning and material variations.

Before

Established semiconductor platforms span 0.1 μeV/Hz to 10 μeV/Hz across GaAs, Si MOS, Si/SiGe, and Ge/SiGe quantum dots.

But

Measured at 20 mK. Charge-qubit coherence estimates assume S1/fγ scaling extrapolates from 1 mHz to 5 GHz. Quantitative charge-noise dephasing bounds do not directly translate to spin or valley qubits.

Tools

hBN-encapsulated bilayer graphene van-der-Waals heterostructures · transport-based noise spectroscopy (Coulomb blockade flank method) · superconducting resonator-based dispersive readout · WSe2/BLG heterostructures

Abstract

Bilayer graphene (BLG) quantum dots (QDs) are a promising platform for semiconductor qubits. However, the low-frequency charge noise that may ultimately limit coherence has remained largely unexplored. Here, we systematically characterize charge noise in gate-defined BLG QDs using transport-based noise spectroscopy. We extract a median amplitude of S_μ^(1/2) (1~Hz) = 1.16~μeV/√Hz, placing BLG well within the range reported for established semiconductor quantum-dot platforms. Across variations in charge occupation, confinement, source-drain bias, and charge-sensor operating conditions, neither the noise amplitude nor the spectral dependence shows a reproducible trend in electrostatic tuning, indicating that we extracted the intrinsic semiconductor noise. Consistent noise levels are further observed in double QDs and confirmed using an independent superconducting resonator-based dispersive readout. Extending the study to BLG devices incorporating transition metal dichalcogenide layers reveals no measurable charge noise increase in weakly proximitized QDs. These results validate BLG as a viable platform for coherent quantum information processing.

item.title: Spin-to-polarization mapping with a coherent quantum dot-cavity receiver
item.description:
Pay dirt new result — Single-photon reflection projects quantum dot electron spin to an eigenstate with 95±2% fidelity, producing orthogonal reflected polarization states with relative Stokes angle α/π=0.95±0.02 (171∘±4∘).

Grade 0.468 · 2.3σ above the day's baseline · matched “Single-shot read-out of an individual electron spin in a quantum dot” · Adrià Medeiros, Vincent Vinel, Eliott Rambeau, Petr Steindl, Elham Mehdi, Manuel Gundín, Clément Millet, Petr Stepanov, Niccolo Somaschi, Aristide Lemaître, Isabelle Sagnes, Olivier Krebs, Pascale Senellart, Dario A. Fioretto, Loïc Lanco

Figure

Angle α/π and Stokes vector purities as a function of delay τ between two reflected photons, showing near-antiparallel polarization states (α≈π) after the transient regime.

Asks

Can spin-induced Kerr rotation in a quantum dot-cavity system realize a bijective one-to-one mapping between spin eigenstates and orthogonal reflected photon polarization states?

But

Liquid Helium cryostat at 4 K; limited by competition between trion radiative lifetime T1(rad)=200±20 ps and spin relaxation time T1(spin)=1.9±0.2 ns.

Tools

negatively charged InGaAs quantum dot · AlGaAs micropillar cavity · time-resolved conditional polarization tomography · continuous-wave laser reflection

Abstract

Coherent light-matter interfaces controllably modifying the state of a photon upon interaction with a stationary qubit are a key resource for implementing deterministic entangling gates for optical quantum technologies. This requires a one-to-one mapping between the state of the scattered photon and that of the embedded qubit. Here, we present an experimental signature of such a bijection by leveraging the spin-induced Kerr rotation present in a low-noise charged quantum dot-micropillar cavity device. Through time-resolved polarization measurements, we project the electron spin to one of its eigenstates with 95±2% fidelity with a single reflected photon detection, and follow the subsequent spin relaxation through the detection of a second reflected photon. We demonstrate that, after a transient regime governed by the trion radiative lifetime, two orthogonal polarization states can be produced, each associated to a given spin eigenstate. While the current results are limited by a timescale competition between electron spin relaxation and trion radiative lifetime, they could be improved using hole spins displaying increased relaxation times. Our work paves the way towards deterministic logic gates exploiting this one-to-one mapping between a spin and the polarization of a scattered photon.

item.title: Extrinsic orbital Edelstein effect from asymmetric scattering
item.description:
Worth a look theory — Disorder-induced asymmetric scattering produces side-jump and skew-scattering orbital Edelstein responses in systems with broken time-reversal symmetry. In a magnetized Rashba 2DEG with Rashba coupling of 1 eV Å, orbital magnetization is about one order of magnitude larger than spin magnetization.

Grade 0.432 · 1.9σ above the day's baseline · matched “Spins in few-electron quantum dots” · Sankar Sarkar, Koushik Ghorai, Amit Agarwal

Figure

Orbital Edelstein susceptibility χz,x components plotted versus chemical potential and exchange-field orientation angle θ.

Asks

How do side-jump and skew-scattering mechanisms modify the orbital Edelstein effect?

But

Weak electric field and disorder treated perturbatively, elastic impurity scattering, intraband small-momentum-transfer approximation, Gaussian noncrossing disorder.

Tools

semiclassical Boltzmann transport theory · first and higher-order Born approximations · magnetized Rashba 2DEG model · magnetic point-group symmetry analysis

Abstract

The generation and manipulation of orbital angular momentum (OAM) by an external electric field constitute one of the central themes of orbitronics. In particular, the electrically induced nonequilibrium OAM polarization, known as the orbital Edelstein effect (OEE), has attracted considerable attention in recent years. While the intrinsic band-geometric mechanism and the role of conventional symmetric impurity scattering in the OEE are well understood, the contribution from disorder-induced asymmetric scattering remains unclear. Here, we develop a semiclassical theory that separates the OEE into intrinsic, Drude, side-jump, and third- and fourth-order skew-scattering channels. Unlike the Drude channel, the intrinsic, side-jump, and skew-scattering responses survive only in systems with broken time-reversal symmetry. We find that in a magnetized Rashba two-dimensional electron gas (2DEG), these disorder-induced mechanisms can substantially exceed the intrinsic contribution. Remarkably, we find that for a system with Rashba coupling of 1 $eV Å$, the orbital magnetization is about one order of magnitude larger than the spin magnetization for the chosen parameters, highlighting the crucial role of orbital degrees of freedom in the Edelstein effect.

item.title: Nanoscale magnetometry via collective many-body dynamics in diamond
item.description:
Worth a look new result — Collective one-axis-twisting dynamics driven by pulsed magnetic-field gradients and dressed-state encoding achieve metrological gains of up to 7.9(2) dB for magnetic signal detection and 8.8(3) dB for magnetic noise sensing.

Grade 0.428 · 1.8σ above the day's baseline · matched “Spins in few-electron quantum dots” · Haoyang Gao, Piotr Put, Nathaniel T. Leitao, Nazli U. Köylüouglu, Andrew Maccabe, Mathew Mammen, Siddharth Dandavate, Lillian B. Hughes Wyatt, Leigh S. Martin, Ania C. Bleszynski Jayich, Hongkun Park, Mikhail D. Lukin

Figure

Measured spin polarization dynamics, twisting/decay rates, and separation distance showing up to 5.4x signal amplification via multi-stage collective one-axis twisting.

Asks

Can dipolar interactions in a solid-state spin ensemble be coherently controlled to provide practical metrological enhancement in nanoscale magnetic sensing accounting for experimental overheads?

Before

Prior NV-ensemble experiments demonstrated ~0.5 dB spin squeezing in sub-ensembles and a 1.067x (0.56 dB) signal enhancement under idealized conditions.

But

Demonstrated with ~8000 spins in bulk diamond; decoherence during gradient winding increases exponentially with wavevector magnitude.

Tools

3D dipolar nitrogen-vacancy center ensemble in bulk diamond · pulsed magnetic field gradients from on-chip microwires · perpendicular bias field dressed-state qubit encoding · one-axis-twisting (OAT) spin-spiral dynamics · Fourier magnetic imaging

Abstract

Many-body dynamics constitutes a promising approach for creating correlations between quantum particles which can be used for applications in sensing and metrology. However, utilizing this potential for substantial gains in practical settings is a challenging task with only a very few applications realized to date. Here, we demonstrate an approach to nanoscale magnetic sensing enabled by strongly interacting electronic spins in a room temperature solid. By coherently controlling collective many-body dynamics of a dipolar ensemble of ∼10⁴ nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centres in diamond with pulsed magnetic field gradients, we demonstrate practical metrological gain up to 7.9(2) dB for magnetic signal detection and 8.8(3) dB for magnetic noise sensing, fully accounting for experimental overheads. Finally, we combine these methods to demonstrate a momentum-space-resolved sensing modality that enables detection of spatially correlated magnetic noise at continuously tunable length scales down to 50 nanometers. These observations open the door toward practical applications of interaction-enhanced quantum sensors for nanoscale biological imaging and material characterization.

item.title: Deterministic nanofabrication for engineering nanowire quantum dot devices
item.description:
Worth a look new method — Deterministic vertical-to-vertical transfer of InAsP/InP nanowire quantum dots via electron-beam-induced deposition of SiOx nano-glue onto pre-fabricated templates. Yields 75% photon extraction efficiency on an Au/SiO2 mirror substrate and 3.6 GHz electrostatic Stark tuning between quadrupolar gates while maintaining g(2)(0)=0.002.

Grade 0.428 · 1.8σ above the day's baseline · matched “Single-shot read-out of an individual electron spin in a quantum dot” · Tarun Patel, Matteo Pennacchietti, Greg Holloway, Stephen R. Harrigan, Sayan Gangopadhyay, Anthony Drouin, Megha Jain, Dan Dalacu, Philip J. Poole, Sasan Vosoogh-Grayli, Michael E. Reimer

Figure

Electron microscopy frames showing the vertical nanowire transfer sequence: mechanical detachment by a tungsten probe at the base (a), followed by EBID SiOx nano-gluing to pick up and secure the nanowire upright onto a target template (b).

Asks

Can vertical nanowire quantum dots be deterministically transferred to pre-patterned templates without losing their upright geometry, optical quality, or single-photon purity?

Before

Nanowire quantum dot pick-and-place transfer relied on van der Waals forces limited to lying-down geometries, while as-grown upright nanowires had a maximum top extraction efficiency limit of 50%.

But

Demonstrated across 8 transferred nanowire devices on mirror templates; Stark tuning tested up to 120 V across a 600 nm gap; spectral shift is reduced compared to theory likely due to screening from background doping in the nanowire.

Tools

dual-beam SEM/FIB with GIS · electron-beam-induced deposition (EBID) · tungsten nanoprobe · InAsP/InP site-selected nanowire quantum dots

Abstract

Semiconductor quantum dots (QDs) are a leading platform for realising bright, wavelength-tunable sources of single and entangled photon pairs for photonic quantum technologies. Site-selected nanowire quantum dots (NWQDs) are a promising platform for fabricating such photonic devices in a scalable manner. However, implementing additional structures around the photonic nanowire while maintaining its vertical growth geometry has remained a challenge. In this work, we develop a deterministic pick-and-place technique to conduct a vertical-to-vertical transfer of NWQDs from the growth substrate to arbitrary templates. Using this transfer technique, we enhance the photon extraction efficiency to 75% by implementing a bottom gold mirror and tune the emission wavelength by 3.6 GHz via implementing electrostatic gates around the QD. Importantly, we measure low-multiphoton probability (g^(2)(0) = 0.002) and high indistinguishability (>80% for +/-100 ps) of the QD emission after the transfer process, yielding high-quality devices. These results demonstrate the repeatability and versatility of the developed transfer technique, which is an enabling step towards scalable single and entangled photon sources.

item.title: Analog quantum simulation of bosonic and anyonic models with flux-driven transmons
item.description:
Worth a look new method — Alternating sinusoidal flux modulation on capacitively coupled transmons enables analog simulation of Bose-Hubbard models with up to three bosons per site without total particle number limits, and provides the first analog transmon protocol for the 1D anyon-Hubbard model with tunable on-site interaction U and statistical phase θ.

Grade 0.426 · 1.8σ above the day's baseline · matched “Quantum computation with quantum dots” · Isak Lyngfelt, Jorge Fernández-Pendás, Göran Johansson, Laura Garciá-Álvarez

Figure

Particle asymmetry Δn at time t=5/J as a function of anyonic statistical phase θ for interaction strengths U/J∈{1,3,5,7}. Driven transmons (markers) reproduce the exact anyon-Hubbard model curves (solid lines).

Asks

Can capacitively coupled flux-tunable transmons perform analog quantum simulation of Bose-Hubbard and anyon-Hubbard models with tunable interactions beyond the two-particle limit?

Before

Parametrically tunable interaction Bose-Hubbard transmon simulations were limited to two particles in total, and anyon models were only simulated digitally.

But

Hilbert space truncated to at most three excitations per site for Bose-Hubbard and two for anyon-Hubbard; decoherence and higher-order flux harmonics neglected.

Tools

flux-tunable transmons · sinusoidal frequency modulation · QuTiP state-vector simulations · rotating wave approximation

Abstract

When quantum particles interact, many-body phenomena that are hard to simulate classically emerge. Quantum analog simulation offers an alternative in which the target system's dynamics is directly realized in controllable quantum hardware. Here, we give a general protocol for simulating the Bose-Hubbard and anyon-Hubbard models using lattices of capacitively coupled flux-tunable transmons. By modulating the transmon frequencies in an alternating pattern, we resonantly drive multiple many-body transitions and can tune the on-site interaction and density-dependent hopping amplitudes for up to three bosons per site, with no additional restriction on the total particle number. By adding phases to the modulation, which renders the transition amplitudes complex-valued, we propose the first simulation protocol for the anyon-Hubbard model with transmons. Numerical simulations of the driven transmon arrays with experimentally realistic parameters reproduce the characteristic dynamics of the target models across a range of interaction strengths and statistical phases, including the interaction-dependent localization and the statistics-dependent asymmetry of the anyonic quantum walk.

item.arxave:abstract: When quantum particles interact, many-body phenomena that are hard to simulate classically emerge. Quantum analog simulation offers an alternative in which the target system's dynamics is directly realized in controllable quantum hardware. Here, we give a general protocol for simulating the Bose-Hubbard and anyon-Hubbard models using lattices of capacitively coupled flux-tunable transmons. By modulating the transmon frequencies in an alternating pattern, we resonantly drive multiple many-body transitions and can tune the on-site interaction and density-dependent hopping amplitudes for up to three bosons per site, with no additional restriction on the total particle number. By adding phases to the modulation, which renders the transition amplitudes complex-valued, we propose the first simulation protocol for the anyon-Hubbard model with transmons. Numerical simulations of the driven transmon arrays with experimentally realistic parameters reproduce the characteristic dynamics of the target models across a range of interaction strengths and statistical phases, including the interaction-dependent localization and the statistics-dependent asymmetry of the anyonic quantum walk.

item.title: Stabilization of dark states in emitter arrays coupled to a half-waveguide
item.description:
Worth a look theory — Applying optimal relative frequency detunings Δj between emitters in a half-waveguide cancels coherent coupling to bright modes, producing exact single-excitation dark states with zero decay rate (γϕ=0) and near-perfect multi-excitation dark states in small arrays.

Grade 0.426 · 1.8σ above the day's baseline · matched “Single-shot read-out of an individual electron spin in a quantum dot” · Oriol Rubies-Bigorda, Susanne F. Yelin, Ana Asenjo-Garcia, Stuart J. Masson

Figure

Level diagrams and decay mechanisms for two emitters in a half-waveguide. Non-zero detuning eliminates coherent cross-coupling between bright and dark Lindbladian eigenstates, isolating the dark state with zero decay rate.

Asks

How can stable, addressable single- and multi-excitation dark states be prepared in small arrays of quantum emitters coupled to a half-waveguide?

But

Markovian approximation (travel time between emitters and mirror is negligible relative to emitter lifetimes), 1D waveguide, two-level emitters.

Tools

Markovian master equation · non-Hermitian Hamiltonian diagonalisation · interference via mirror boundary conditions · engineered emitter detuning profiles

Abstract

The radiative properties of quantum emitters are profoundly influenced by their electromagnetic environment. When coupled to a waveguide terminated at one end by a mirror, distant emitters interact strongly via virtual photon exchange, leading to collective superradiant and subradiant states with enhanced or suppressed decay rates. We demonstrate that applying optimal frequency shifts to each emitter enables the formation of perfect single-excitation dark states (i.e. states with zero decay rate) and near-perfect multi-excitation dark states in small ensembles. These collective states can be deterministically prepared with high fidelity using classical driving fields or few-photon pulses propagating along the waveguide. These results, readily implementable in superconducting qubit platforms, open new avenues for quantum information storage, networking and control of light.

item.title: Tuning Andreev reflection and conductance in proximitized nanowires through the spin-orbit field direction
item.description:
Worth a look theory — In the topologically trivial phase of a proximitized nanowire junction, varying the spin-orbit field misalignment angle ϕSO from 0 to π tunes the finite-energy Andreev reflection coefficient from Rhe≃0.87 down to complete suppression Rhe≃4⋅10−4, and conductance at eV=0.1Δ0 from ≈1.74e2/h to ≈10−3e2/h. Zero-energy values remain fixed by the topological invariant.

Grade 0.417 · 1.7σ above the day's baseline · matched “Charge Noise Spectroscopy Using Coherent Exchange Oscillations in a Singlet-Tri…” · Leonardo Musca, Fabrizio Dolcini

Figure

Plots show the bulk excitation spectra (a), the energy-dependent Andreev reflection coefficient Rhe(E) (b), and the nonlinear differential conductance G(V) (c) in the trivial phase (EZ=0.8Δ0) for spin-orbit misalignment angles ϕSO=0,π/2,π. Tuning ϕSO strongly suppresses both Rhe and G(V) at finite energy/bias while leaving zero-bias values at zero.

Asks

How do spatial inhomogeneities in the direction of the Rashba spin-orbit field across a normal-superconductor nanowire junction affect Andreev reflection and conductance?

But

Single-channel nanowire model with axial Zeeman field 𝐛=(bx,0,0) and transverse spin-orbit fields lying purely in the y-z plane; no inelastic scattering.

Tools

Bogoliubov-de Gennes Hamiltonian · Scattering matrix method · Effective mass model

Abstract

We investigate the Andreev reflection (AR) and the nonlinear conductance in a normal-superconductor junction realized with a proximitized semiconductor nanowire exposed to a magnetic field along its axis. We show that, while at zero energy the AR coefficient is determined by the topological phase of the superconducting side of the junction, at finite energy the AR is strongly affected by the directions of the Rashba spin-orbit field characterizing the normal and the proximitized sides. The tunability of the AR and the nonlinear conductance as a function of the spin-orbit misalignment angle is particularly pronounced when the proximitized side is in the topologically trivial phase. The spin-orbit field direction is revealed to be an efficient knob to control the electron transport through the hybrid junction, realizing an electrically widely tunable device. The implementation in realistic setups is discussed.
